chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Mālik ibn Aʿyan, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman in postnatal bleeding: may her husband have intercourse with her while she is still in her nifās from the blood?

He عليه السلام said: Yes, when there has passed for her, from the day she gave birth, a period equal to the number of days of her menstrual habit, then she adds one precautionary day; after that, there is no harm in her husband having intercourse with her. He instructs her to perform ghusl, so she performs ghusl, then he may have intercourse with her if he wishes.

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath required before resuming certain acts
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she adds an extra precautionary period
key_terms.عِدَّةِ حَيْضِهَا: the known number of days of her menstrual habit
key_terms.نِفَاسِهَا: her state of postnatal bleeding after childbirth

ai.seo_question: When may a husband have intercourse with his wife after childbirth in the case of nifās?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intercourse with a woman experiencing postnatal bleeding. It states that after the length of her usual menstrual period has passed from childbirth, plus one additional precautionary day, the husband may approach her after she performs ghusl.
